head: d1b841b
target: Grade agent runs from files: a scenario scripts the steps, the run lands as a result directory, and the report judges engine invariants and model behaviors from those files.
incidental: the CLI's usage text and flag defaults
the npm bin entry and script
the file names inside a result directory
the test scenario fixture and its plugin shims
the guard update in the import-boundary test

questions.prompt: The report of a fresh run comes from reading its own result files back from disk. Why not grade the run it still holds in memory?

options.label: The files alone carry everything a grade needs; a later grader reads the same files.
Reading back is cheaper than keeping the whole run in memory.
Grading from files keeps the report safe if the process dies.
It proves the scrub left no raw secret value in the files.

key_points: The result files are the whole input to a grade; the run in memory is not consulted.
A later grader reads the same files, so the run's verdict and the grader's cannot drift.
Every run exercises the same load-back the later grader relies on.

questions.prompt: A report shows one failed invariant, one failed behavior, and a cost figure. Which of these hold?

options.label: The failed invariant is an engine bug, and it fails the run.
The failed behavior is a model miss, and it never fails the run.
The cost figure is reported and never judged.
The failed behavior must be fixed in the engine before the next run.

key_points: Invariants are engine properties every run must keep; a fail is an engine bug and gates the run.
Behaviors are bets on the model, reported as rates, and never gate the run.
Cost is reported, never judged; the cached share of prompt tokens feeds the tool-mode decision.

questions.prompt: A prompt's expectation says the model must call a tool right after it enables the plugin. The model never enables the plugin. How is the expectation judged?

options.label: Skipped: no chance to show, and left out of the behavior's rate.
Skipped: no chance to show, but counted as a miss in the rate.
Failed: the model broke the scenario's rule.
Passed: nothing went wrong in the engine.

key_points: A behavior whose precondition never happened is skipped, not failed.
A skip is left out of the rate, so rates count only real chances.
Each behavior owns its own skip rule, because it owns its precondition.

questions.prompt: The test scenario's weather plugin echoes the run's declared secret into its tool results. Suppose the engine fails to redact that value. What does the run show?
key_points: The scrub replaces the raw value with a mark naming the secret, in every string of the run log.
The written files hold the mark, never the raw value.
The invariant on leaks reads the marks and fails the run as an engine bug.
The echoing plugin makes every run test redaction on a value that really flowed.

questions.prompt: Which of these stop a run before its first model call?

options.label: A field the scenario format does not define
A tool name that no loaded plugin provides
A declared secret with no value in the environment
A prompt the model is likely to fail

key_points: Unknown fields are problems, so a misspelled word cannot silently drop a run's expectations.
Names the expectations rely on are checked against the plugins in effect at that step.
An unset secret or model key stops the run up front.
Every problem is collected, each named at its place in the scenario file.

questions.prompt: Why does the writer build a run's files in a sibling directory and move it into place at the end?

options.label: A result directory holds a whole run or does not exist.
Readers grade the files while the run is still writing them.
Moving a directory is faster than writing its files in place.
The checks cannot read files that are still open.

key_points: The move is the commit: no reader ever sees a half-written run.
A crash leaves a sibling marked partial, never a result directory.

questions.prompt: A new expectation arrives: the model must call two named tools in a given order, within one prompt. Where does it go, and what changes?
key_points: It lands in the scenario format: one new check with its own fields.
Its judging is one new case beside the existing behaviors, with its own skip rule.
The runner, the result files and the invariants stay untouched.

questions.prompt: A person interrupts the run during its third of five prompts. The run still writes its result directory. Which of these hold?

options.label: The directory holds the steps that ran, with the aborted prompt last.
The report marks the run as stopped early, not as an engine bug.
Behaviors on prompts four and five are skipped.
The aborted prompt's behaviors fail, because the model never answered.

key_points: An interrupt ends the run where it stands, not with a thrown error.
Every step that ran is written and graded, the aborted one included.
The report separates a stopped run from an engine bug.
Behaviors with no chance to show are skipped, not failed.
